profile_text.body:
The Algorithmic Justice League is a nonprofit founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States. Its website describes a mission to raise awareness about the impacts of AI, equip advocates with empirical research, build the voice and choice of the most impacted communities, and galvanize researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases. The organization states that AI systems are used to decide who gets hired, the quality of medical treatment, and whether someone becomes a suspect in a police investigation, and that unchecked AI can amplify racism, sexism, ableism, and other forms of discrimination.

The organization does not list commercial AI products. Its public work focuses on advocacy and research around equitable and accountable AI, civil rights, and biometric rights. The website highlights the expansion of facial recognition technology by TSA in airports and encourages travelers to consider opting out. It also points to the documentary Coded Bias, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020, as an account of the organization's origins and of people affected by harmful technology.

Available records associate the organization with Massachusetts legal or regulatory matters, with 191 entries. No products or court cases are listed in the available facts.
